state.objective: Study how /tests can end up with all test logic and scheduling expressed in Can. Retaining the old host harness is explicitly unwanted. No code migration is being performed in this investigation. Go-based compilation and Bun-backed primitives remain infrastructure; relocating scenario-specific checks into those primitives is not an acceptable conversion.
state.capabilities: The language already supplies callable code, mandatory asserts, invocation-local when tables with FIFO order, reusable scenarios and templates, checks::require, codecs for JSON, files APIs and process::run. Normal programs may perform real I/O. Subprocess calls configure directory/environment/stdin, cap elapsed time and stream sizes, and return both streams, code and signal. Assertions instead reject actual platform effects. General finally syntax is absent; runtime ownership can close registered resources, but killing a process cannot certify that its cleanup finished.
state.runner: Existing canlc assert validates all source, optionally selects roots, and supervises isolated execution with --assert-jobs and wall-time limits before producing structured results. Existing canlc run verifies the program assertions and builds/publishes before main. A native multi-project integration-suite registry and execution report have not been implemented. Compile-negative projects can already be treated as subprocess inputs and checked through status/stderr. Public structured semantic diagnostics would require a CLI facade over available diagnostic machinery.
state.gaps: One-shot process::run does not publish a live child resource for later communication/signaling and lacks arbitrary extra inherited file descriptors. The legacy tests depend on fd-3 secrets, crash versus graceful termination, restart, ports, owned workspaces and safe abandoned-run reclamation. Standard status/header/body HTTP tests can use named fetch http::response<bytes::buffer> now. Wire corruption, deliberately slow writes and abrupt connection loss still lack a corresponding control surface.
state.browser: Current browser::* calls serve in-page application DOM programming. External automation is presently Playwright code exercising Chromium/WebKit/Firefox navigation, gestures/events, network overrides, console/DOM evidence and hostile inputs. Some Bun qualification checks require direct native access and synthetic proxy/thenable values unavailable to normal Can data. A faithful port must preserve an observation channel distinct from the production mechanism being validated.
state.constraints: There is no external compatibility constituency. Preserve each meaningful obligation, without promising old layout or count equality. Disk is limited to 256 GB and load must stay bounded: no broad builds, benchmarking, lasting personal caches or dependency clones. Build the candidate once for reuse, restrict jobs/output/time and attach cleanup as soon as resources are acquired. The directory also holds non-executable fixtures and historical records. Because the candidate compiles Can, it could corrupt a self-compiled test runner; a maintained known-good executable prevents that shared failure path but costs upkeep.

execution.instructions: Which architecture is the strongest first prototype for the stated Can-only test-ownership goal, accounting for existing offline guarantees and the cost of expanding the language? Judge future direction rather than whether gaps are already solved.

criteria.suite_program: Use a dedicated Can main program and ordinary function cases to compose existing process/files/JSON/checks facilities. Introduce only demonstrated generic lifetime or observation gaps, assert its deterministic internals, and add a canlc test launcher later if useful.
criteria.live_assertions: Make live effects a separately selected assertion mode. Extend worker/report rules and keep those cases outside routine build verification, while Can code continues to define orchestration.
criteria.test_declarations: Add a dedicated testing declaration surface that owns case discovery and suite boundaries, implemented with a Can suite coordinator and native platform operations; retain attached assertions as they are.
criteria.undetermined: Withhold an architectural preference pending one targeted investigation that supplies a missing deciding fact.

browser.instructions: Choose the most productive first step for replacing browser harness code while requiring Can-defined scenarios/verdicts and equivalent real-engine evidence.

criteria.typed_driver: Expose typed maintained calls to the upstream Playwright engine. Keep backend work limited to reusable automation mechanics and observed results, with test actions and expected outcomes specified in Can rather than embedded test procedures.
criteria.can_protocol: Develop browser-protocol control directly in Can on HTTP/WebSocket and owned process facilities, then qualify all used protocol capabilities on the three engines and maintain that client.
criteria.capability_spike: Measure feasibility with a small non-performance experiment covering the hardest required browser actions; use the observed gaps to choose between Playwright-backed calls and a native Can protocol client.

bootstrap.instructions: Recommend the default execution provenance for testing a compiler with Can-authored suites, balancing trustworthy failure detection with laptop resource limits.

criteria.known_good: Select a digest-verified suite executable produced by a trusted compiler to exercise the candidate and compare independent expectations; deliberately rebuild that executable when runner changes are accepted.
criteria.candidate_only: Let the candidate compile and run its own suite, using failure-seeding and fixed expected vectors together with the remaining compiler/runtime unit tests outside /tests to counter shared defects.
criteria.dual: Execute the suite both from a trusted build and from a fresh candidate build on every run and contrast observations, accepting the duplicated execution and compilation expense.
